destination.name: Hunter Valley
destination.tagline: A wine region of cellar doors, themed gardens and heritage villages, a weekend trip from Sydney.
destination.description: The Hunter Valley is New South Wales's wine region, one of the first planted in Australia, in the early 19th century, and now home to over 150 wineries. Around Pokolbin the vineyards and small villages have no single centre, with Cessnock the service town and Maitland, Morpeth and Wollombi holding heritage buildings. Semillon and Shiraz are the best-known wines, and Watagans National Park's rainforest lies an hour from Newcastle. The Hunter has been overtaken by the Riverina as NSW's biggest producer and makes about 3% of Australia's wine.
whyVisit: Taste wine at Pokolbin cellar doors
Hike to waterfalls in Watagans National Park

goodToKnow.title: Gardens entry
goodToKnow.detail: Hunter Valley Gardens costs $39 for adults, opens 9 am to 5 pm with last entry at 4 pm, and is closed on Christmas Day.

goodToKnow.title: Cessnock fills up
goodToKnow.detail: Wikivoyage notes Cessnock can be booked out, in which case Maitland is a workable base; tours with pick-up from Newcastle or Sydney are an alternative to driving between cellar doors.

goodToKnow.title: Morpeth is a weekend stop
goodToKnow.detail: Morpeth is best visited Thursday to Sunday, and cellar doors typically open about 10 am to 5 pm.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}: travel guides favour autumn for harvest activity and mild weather, spring brings budding vines and the biggest crowds, and heavy rain and storms are more common in summer and autumn.
